applications.title: AI-Assisted Web Developer
applications.coverLetterText:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to apply for the AI-Assisted Web Developer role at Amped Marketing. The way you have framed this role — AI is not a nice-to-have, it is the core of how you work — is exactly how I operate, and I want to be direct about what that looks like in practice.

My AI Development Workflow

I use Claude Code for architecture decisions, component scaffolding, and refactoring complex logic. I use Cursor for in-file editing with live context. I use v0 to rapidly prototype UI patterns from prompts or design references. I use Figma Dev Mode and Figma Make to extract design intent and generate baseline code from layouts. Then I audit and clean every output before it touches a client's production environment — because I know what AI gets wrong: semantic structure, mobile edge cases, accessibility attributes, and anything that requires understanding the actual user's context. That combination is what lets me move fast and ship clean.

Production Delivery

In my freelance practice — callcatchai.online, primelayertrades.com, hereraspreadsheets.com — I have built and shipped production web applications including AdvisoryCloud 3.0 (React 18, Supabase, PWA, deployed to Vercel with CI/CD, real users, real data) and a full-stack logistics tracking application — both built from Figma wireframes to live production in days, not weeks. I have managed WordPress and Shopify builds for all three clients: theme customization, plugin integration, storefront configuration, and ongoing maintenance. I run full QA cycles — Lighthouse, cross-browser, mobile responsiveness, semantic markup review — before every client delivery.

Agency Pace

I am built for concurrent project environments. Managing multiple clients simultaneously on different schedules and timelines is how I have worked for the past several years. I understand what it means to move a project from concept to launch quickly without cutting quality corners on the things that actually matter — page speed, accessibility, and code that can be maintained after the fact.

I would be glad to share examples of recent projects and walk through exactly how AI fit into each stage of the build. I look forward to discussing the role.

Sincerely,
Alexander Tobin
